study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative modelling of brain function abnormalities in complex pathology needs the whole brain

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Propose and evaluate FUNCOIN, a whole-brain normative modeling approach for resting-state functional connectivity that relates component magnitudes to age and sex, and test whether it identifies individual-level abnormalities in bipolar disorder and Parkinson's disease using UK Biobank.

rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: We use rsfMRI data from UKB (N >60,000 people)... training data, N=32,000 ... test data, N=14,000 ... BD (N=101) and PD (N=132).

caa6_deviation_metric.reason: Individual deviations quantified via Z-scores relative to normative model with |z|>2 as outlier; group-level comparisons via outlier proportions and counts.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Permutation tests with Fisher's exact test for outlier proportions; Mann–Whitney U for outlier count distributions; Spearman correlations for relations to counts; FDR correction using Benjamini–Yekutieli; implemented with SciPy and scikit-learn.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Whole-brain normative modeling (FUNCOIN) identified significantly elevated abnormal FC patterns in BD and PD that localized edgewise models missed; PD abnormalities were detectable up to ~8 years before diagnosis; BD exhibited two distinct deviation subgroups.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Out-of-sample validation on 14,000 healthy subjects supported the normative model. In PD, 9.1% had Z1<-2 vs. ~2.3% expected by chance (padj=0.002). In BD, 6.9% had Z2<-2 (padj=0.046); 7.9% had Z1>2 (did not survive FDR, padj=0.09). Among PD subjects scanned up to 7.8 years before diagnosis, 9.3% were Z1<-2 outliers. BD subjects separated into two subgroups: none had both Z1>2 and Z2<-2, suggesting distinct deviation patterns. Edgewise analyses suffered from multiple-comparisons issues (no edges significant after BY correction).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: FUNCOIN integrates dimensionality reduction with covariance regression to avoid mass-univariate testing and to improve specificity and scalability; components map onto interpretable networks; sensitivity analyses including site covariate yielded consistent primary components.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Preprint; reliance on a single dataset (UKB) without external validation; limited reporting on image-level QC and motion control; site assessed but not modeled in main results; model captures linear/heteroscedastic dependence on covariates and may miss nonlinearities beyond age/sex.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: UKB rsfMRI with 55-ICA parcellation; two FUNCOIN components trained on 32k healthy and validated on 14k healthy; clinical BD (n=101) and PD (n=132) within UKB. Visualization with FSL fsleyes. Supplementary shows no apparent site effect across 4 sites and details implementation (GitHub link).
